# dsh-unified-model
**Switch model and reasoning effort across every DeepSeek Harness session at once — one control, all
conversations, effort included.**
中文
DeepSeek Harness stores the model choice **per session**. The shipped default-model setting only cov
ers sessions that have not chosen one yet, and `/model` only ever changes the session you are in. So
there is no built-in way to move a whole session history onto one model/effort pair at once.
This plugin adds that missing control to the composer row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
In a narrow window the button collapses to its glyph so it stops competing for room with the model p
arrow window the button collapses to its glyph so it stops competing for room with the model picker:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The same control stays reachable either way — the full name lives in the button's `title` and `aria-
label`, so the icon-only form is not an unlabelled mystery.
Open it, pick a provider, a model and a thinking effort, and choose the scope:
| Option | Effect |

| **Every session** | writes the selection into every session that can hold its own |
| **Every othe

r session** | same, but leaves the session you are looking at untouched |
| **Also make this the def
ault** | additionally writes the deployment default, so sessions created later start on it |
A live `done/total` counter runs while the batch is in flight, and the result reports what changed,
what already matched, and what failed.
## Why effort is included
Most "apply a model to all sessions" attempts stop at the model, because effort looks like it belong
s to a different layer. It does not:

- `sessionController.selectModel()` takes `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort? }`.
- The selection i
t commits is appended to the session log as a `model/selection` event, and that event's schema **car

ries `reasoningEffort`**.
- The `modelSelection` projection re-reads it, and `selectionFor()` restor
es it after a restart, so the effort survives.
Verified on a live profile: a written session log contains
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That is why this plugin compares `provider` **and** `model` **and** `reasoningEffort` when it decide
s whether a session already matches. A plugin that compares only the first two will report success w
hile silently leaving effort unapplied.
## Scope and limits
| Case | Behaviour |

| Ordinary sessions | **Updated** — the target of the control |
| Subagent sessions | **Not touched.
** They follow their parent's routing and the host rejects per-session selection for them. Counted s

eparately in the result so they are never mistaken for failures |
| A session already carrying the t
arget selection | **Skipped**, no write. A repeat click on an already-unified history finishes in mi

lliseconds |
| A session whose log is corrupt or locked by another process | Reported as **failed**
with the host's own reason, and the rest of the batch continues |
The batch runs **on the Host**, not in the browser, so closing the tab does not interrupt it. The cl
ient half only starts the run and polls its progress.
## How it works
It does not patch a shipped plugin, rewrite session logs, or edit projection caches. It calls the sa
me public host API the built-in `/model` dialog calls:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Because the write path is the official one, session state stays in the official format, uninstalling
changes nothing, and a future Harness that renames these methods costs you this plugin only — never
the rest of the app.
Three route exist, all behind the composition's connection trust fence:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Read before write
`selectModel` resumes each cold session, which is by far the most expensive part of the operation. S
o the plugin reads every session's selection from `list()` first and skips matching ones. Measured o
n a 55-session profile: the first run wrote 36 sessions in **2.7 s**; the immediate repeat skipped 5
3 and finished in **56 ms**.
### Validate before writing
An unknown model or an effort the model does not publish makes the adapter reject the request. Both
are checked against `modelCatalog()` **before** the first session is touched, so a typo fails the re
quest instead of failing 60 sessions one by one:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The client offers exactly the levels the model publishes, so the two never disagree.

## Configuration
None. The control appears in the composer row; there is nothing to set up.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0` or newer.
- The web UI (the control lives in a composer slot).
